title: ‘10 Things I Hate About You’ Cast Reunites During Julia Stiles’ Heath Ledger ‘DWTS’ Dedication Night Tribute
summary: Julia Stiles gave us 10 things to love about her “Dancing With the Stars” Dedication Night performance.
story: Julia Stiles gave us 10 things to love about her “Dancing With the Stars” Dedication Night performance.

During the Oct. 20 episode, Stiles and partner Ezra Sosa performed a heartfelt contemporary routine set to “Can’t Take My Eyes Off You” by Frankie Valli. The performance was in honor of her late “10 Things I Hate About You” co-star Heath Ledger, who died of an accidental overdose in 2008.
Fans of the film know the song very well, as it’s the one that Ledger’s character Patrick sings to Stiles’ Kat while she’s at soccer practice and he’s trying to make her go on a date with him.
Stiles said during rehearsals that she wishes she could call up Ledger and tell him how much people still love their movie. She said their dance would show his “lust for life.”
The performance was emotional and uplifting. It gave nods to Ledger and the film, before it ended with Stiles putting a flower on the steps.
A photo of Stiles and Ledger was shown on the screen, as her iconic “I Hate You” speech from the film was heard.
Fans got a bigger surprise when the “10 Things I Hate About You” cast appeared on the ballroom floor.
Andrew Keegan, Susan May Pratt, Larisa Oleynik, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Larisa Oleynik and Gabrielle Union surrounded Stiles as the routine ended.
The cast had also created a video before the episode, sharing how they were in attendance to support their girl.
Stiles had previously teased “some special surprises.”

“Making ‘10 Things I Hate About You’ with him was such a special moment in time,” she said in a clip shared days before. “It’s amazing that people still care about that movie, and it’s just sad that we can’t celebrate it with him.”
Sosa also expressed how honored and grateful he was for the opportunity.

“We felt like this routine is so important, not just to honor Heath, but to celebrate the joy and capture his essence in that time that you guys had together filming ‘10 Things I Hate About You,’” he said.
Released in 1999, the teen rom-com is loosely based on William Shakespeare’s “The Taming of the Shrew.” Set in Seattle, Washington, it follows sisters Kat (Stiles) and Bianca Stratford (Oleynik).

Desperate to have a more exciting social life and go to prom, Bianca teams up with new student Cameron (Gordon-Levitt) — who is head-over-heels for her — to find someone to date Kat, an outspoken and independent feminist. Enter Patrick, the bad boy from Australia, who gets paid to woo Kat.
To prepare for the big night, Stiles and Sosa re-created Kat and Patrick’s memorable paintball scene.
They also did the voiceover where Stiles took over Ledger’s lines, while Sosa did hers.
Ledger leaves behind an incredible legacy and body of work that include “The Dark Knight,” for which he won the best supporting actor Oscar, “A Knight’s Tale,” “The Patriot” and “Brokeback Mountain.”
The actor was found dead in January of 2008 in his Manhattan apartment after his accidental overdose. He welcomed daughter Matilda Rose Ledger, now 20, with actor Michelle Williams.

title: Tyler Cameron Reveals He’s Having a Baby With Fiancée Tate Madden During ‘DWTS’ Dedication Night Routine
summary: This just might be a “Dancing With the Stars” first!
story: This just might be a “Dancing With the Stars” first!
During his Dedication Night performance on Oct. 20, Tyler Cameron revealed that he and fiancée Tate Madden are expecting their first child together.
The moment happened as he danced a contemporary alongside partner Sharna Burgess dedicated to his late mom.
During rehearsals, he got emotional saying that weddings make him super emotional because he won’t be able to dance with his mom at his. He then reflected on marrying Madden soon.
While dancing to “Supermarket Flowers” by Ed Sheeran, voiceover of Cameron reading a letter to his mom was heard. During one moment, he revealed that he is going to be a father.

“You would’ve loved the woman I’m gonna marry ... she’s going to be the most incredible momma, just like you,” he said. “And we’re going to have a baby. I can’t believe I’m going to be a dad. Wish you were here. Hope that I make you proud.”
Madden joined Cameron on the dance floor and they cradled her baby bump as the news was announced.
As they ended their dance, Alfonso Ribeiro did a gender reveal and pink confetti exploded in the ballroom.
“It’s a girl!” Alfonso Ribeiro announced, as he asked the couple how they were feeling.
“This is incredible. I get to be a girl dad, what a gift,” Cameron said. “I get to be her husband soon and the father of our beautiful baby.”
The judges were emotional after the performance and reveal, with Bruno Tonioli saying, “You were dancing with three hearts, beating as one.”

title: How Val Chmerkovskiy’s Absence Was Addressed on ‘DWTS’ Dedication Night
summary: “Dancing With the Stars” was missing prominent pro Val Chmerkovskiy during Dedication Night. Here is how the show addressed his absence.
story: “Dancing With the Stars” was missing prominent pro Val Chmerkovskiy during Dedication Night.
His absence was briefly mentioned at the top of the Oct. 20 episode by co-Alfonso Ribeiro, who noted that Chmerkovskiy’s partner, Jenna Dewan, was paired with someone new this week.
“As you can see Alan Bersten is with Jenna Dewan because Val is not with us this week,” Ribeiro said, before the competition continued.

Bersten is filling in for Val Chmerkovskiy after being suspended for referencing Will Smith slapping Chris Rock at the 2022 Oscars when reacting to “DWTS” judge Carrie Ann Inaba’s critiques about his wife, fellow pro Jenna Johnson during the Oct. 13 episode.
His absence was quickly mentioned at the top of the episode by co-host Alfonso Ribeiro, who noted, “As you can see Alan Bersten is with Jenna Dewan because Val is not with us this week.”
Then during Dewan’s package, which shows how she prepared for Dedication Night, Bersten acknowledged filling in for Chmerkovskiy.
“First and foremost, I know it’s a really unusual situation,” Bersten tells Dewan. “But I feel so honored to step in and help this week.”
They then dig into Dewan dedicating her dance to her mom, Nancy, who has supported her in achieving her dreams.
“I want to make sure this dance is so special, not only for you but for your mom,” Bersten says, as they rehearsed their Viennese waltz to “Unchained Melody” by The Righteous Brothers.
Following their performance, which was praised by the judges, Dewan thanked Bersten as they received a 37 out of 40.
Here’s everything to know about Chmerkovskiy’s suspension and Bersten filling in.
What Did Val Chmerkovskiy Say That Got Him Suspended?

During the Oct. 13 episode of “DWTS,” Inaba pointed out a lift in Johnson’s samba routine with Harry Shum Jr. Many on the ballroom floor and online — Chmerkovskiy included — did not like the way Inaba expressed herself when noting that traditional competitive Latin dances do not include lifts.

“A lift is, I just need to say it,” she said, reading off the definition from her notes. “Any movement during which one of the dancers has both feet off the floor at the same time with the assistance or support of their partner. Yeah, lift.”
In a since-deleted message on social media, Chmerkovskiy wrote, “You almost saw Fresh Prince enter the ballroom last night,” referring to Smith’s infamous Oscar moment.
He issued an apology on Oct. 15 following backlash from his comments, saying he reached out to Inaba, according to E! News.
Chmerkovskiy Was Then Suspended
On Oct. 17, in a statement to NBC News, BBC Studios announced the dancer’s one-week suspension.

“The well-being of everyone who works on ‘Dancing with the Stars’ is non-negotiable,” the statement reads. “Val’s social media post was inappropriate and does not reflect the values or standards expected of anyone connected with the show. As a result, he will not participate in next week’s show.”
TODAY.com confirmed on Oct. 20 that the dancer’s suspension was not because of an HR complaint that was filed by Inaba.
Chmerkovskiy Reacted to His Suspension
In a statement posted on his Instagram story, Chmerkovskiy confirmed that he would not be participating in Dedication Week.

“In a moment where my instinct was to defend my wife, I made a poor decision to reference a meme to ‘keep my wife’s name’ out of the conversation, without stopping to think through what else that reference could imply,” he wrote, adding, “which was genuinely never my intention.”
He noted that “Carrie Ann certainly didn’t deserve to get caught in the middle of my bad judgment, and I hate that she was.”

“The last thing I want is to become a distraction from an important week or from the incredible work my dance partner Jenna Dewan is putting in,” he wrote, before concluding, “Please send Carrie Ann, Jenna, and the whole ‘DWTS’ family lots of love during Dedication Night. I’ll be watching and cheering everyone on!!”
Inaba has yet to respond to Chmerkovskiy’s latest statement.
Alan Bersten Returns to the Ballroom
For Season 35, Bersten was paired with award-winning chef Giada De Laurentiis. They were eliminated during the second week of the competition.
The 32-year-old dancer is a Mirrorball Trophy winner, winning Season 28 with his partner, former Bachelorette Hannah Brown.
In an update on social media on Oct. 19, Dewan shared video of her mom in rehearsals with her and Bersten.
“She has been the biggest support system throughout my entire life,” Dewan says in the clip, sharing how her mom showed her the “true values in life” and how to rise to the occasion and challenges.

She also shared how she owes everything to her mom, who got her into dance and supported her. “She was a single mom. She went through some really hard things when I was younger,” the “Step Up” star said, adding that this routine is “my gift to her.”
The video also showed the actor’s mom dancing with Bersten.

title: Tatyana Ali and Alfonso Ribeiro Bring the Tears and Smiles Honoring Late James Avery During ‘DWTS’ Dedication Night
summary: Tatyana Ali brought all the feels to the “Dancing With the Stars” ballroom floor on Dedication Night. She was joined by TV brother Alfonso Ribeiro.
story: Tatyana Ali brought all the feels to the “Dancing With the Stars” ballroom floor on Dedication Night.
The actor and partner Jan Ravnik performed a Viennese waltz to “(You Don’t Know) How Glad I Am” by Nancy Wilson to honor the late James Avery during the Oct. 20 episode.
Avery portrayed Ali and “DWTS” co-host Alfonso Ribeiro’s on-screen father Philip Banks for six seasons on “The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air” from 1990 to 1996.
The routine was extra special as Ribeiro joined his TV sister and longtime friend on the dance floor for a special one-on-one moment that got the crowd emotional.
Calling him a “father figure,” Ali expressed her love for Avery during rehearsals. “I loved him a lot.”

Ali began her performance wearing a gorgeous peach-colored gown while seated on a couch. Ravnik then swept her on her feet as they elegantly waltzed across the floor. Midway through her performance, Ribeiro, who won Season 19 of “DWTS,” joined her as they closed the routine.
Their performance ended with the two holding hands and embracing as a photo of Avery was seen on the screen behind them.
The judges praised their heartfelt routine, with Carrie Ann Inaba saying she felt honored to witness the longtime friends dancing together.
The couple received a 32 out of 40, their best scores of the night.
Days before Dedication Night, Ali revealed that she would actually be singing Wilson’s song and dance to a pre-recorded version of it.
“We’re dancing to a Nancy Wilson song that I’m going to sing. I’m going to pre-record it,” she shared. “And I just hope ... you all feel how much that we love him.”
She said that Avery was a “lover of jazz” and that Wilson was one of his favorite artists.

“James Avery played Uncle Phil on ‘The Fresh Prince of Bel Air.’ He means a lot to fans of the show. He meant a lot to me. He was a mentor to me, a teacher to me,” Ali said in the video. “He was the heart of our show in so many ways. He loved the arts, and he taught me about all of the artists he thought I needed to know.”
“I wouldn’t be who I am today as a performer, as a woman, without him being in my life. And I want to honor him,” she continued. “I get to perform with Alfonso to honor James.”
“The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air” followed Will Smith as he moved from West Philadelphia to his rich relatives’ Bel-Air mansion. Ali’s Ashley and Ribeiro’s Carlton were Will’s cousins.
Avery’s Uncle Phil was the stern, yet loving father figure Will always needed. The iconic actor died at the age of 68 in 2013.

title: Val Chmerkovskiy Hit With One-Week Suspension on ‘DWTS,’ But Not Because of an HR Complaint
summary: Val Chmerkovskiy is not participating in the upcoming episode of “Dancing With The Stars.”
story: Val Chmerkovskiy is not participating in the upcoming episode of “Dancing With The Stars.”

The show announced Oct. 17 that Chmerkovskiy, a pro on the competition who’s currently paired with actor Jenna Dewan, had been suspended for a week. He would ultimately be missing the Dedication Night Oct. 20 episode.
Ahead of the new “DWTS” episode, TODAY.com confirmed that the dancer was non suspended because of an HR complaint filed by judge Carrie Ann Inaba.

Instead, it comes after Chmerkovskiy found himself in hot water last week when he posted a status on TikTok that appeared to reference Will Smith’s notorious altercation with Chris Rock at the 2022 Oscars. The pro had been reacting to the harsh critique that Inaba gave his wife, fellow pro Jenna Johnson who’s paired up with actor Harry Shum Jr.
“You almost saw Fresh Prince enter the ballroom last night,” Chmerkovskiy wrote in the since-deleted status seen by NBC News.
In a statement sent to NBC News on Oct. 17, BBC Studios, the production company behind “DWTS,” said that the “well-being of everyone who works on Dancing with the Stars is non-negotiable.”

“Val’s social media post was inappropriate and does not reflect the values or standards expected of anyone connected with the show,” the statement said. “As a result, he will not participate in next week’s show.”
Chmerkovskiy responded to the news of his suspension by posting an apology to his Instagram story. The dancer wrote that he initially intended to “defend my wife.”

“I made a poor decision to reference a meme to ‘keep my wife’s name’ out of the conversation, without stopping to think through what else that reference could imply, which was genuinely never my intention,” he wrote, referencing Smith’s words to Rock amid the Oscars spat, “Keep my wife’s name out of your f------ mouth.”
Chmerkovskiy added: “Carrie Ann certainly didn’t deserve to get caught in the middle of my bad judgment, and I hate that she was.”
He also had some well wishes for those on the show.
“Please send Carrie Ann, Jenna, and the whole DWTS family lots of love during Dedication Night,” he wrote. “I’ll be watching and cheering everyone on!!”
Inaba has not responded publicly to Chmerkovskiy’s apology or suspension.
Instead of performing with Chmerkovskiy, Dewan will be dancing with pro Alan Bersten in a number that’s dedicated to her mother.

Things got heated amid the Oct. 13 episode of “DWTS” when Inaba accused Johnson of incorporating a lift into her samba routine with Shum. The Latin style of dance traditionally prohibits the move — something that the judge has enforced in the past.
While Johnson, looking confused, asked, “Lift?” Inaba returned with an immediate response.

“A lift is, I just need to say it,” she said before reading off of a sheet of paper with the printed definition. “Any movement during which one of the dancers has both feet off the floor at the same time with the assistance or support of their partner. Yeah. Lift.”
Later on in the episode, Johnson appeared to take the criticism well.
“I will take it, sure,” she said.
Chmerkovskiy has previously apologized for his TikTok status. On Oct. 15, he posted on his Instagram story that he had reached out to Inaba directly to apologize.

“I recognize that I am in a fortunate position to have a platform and to be a role model to some, and I need to treat that with more care by actively pausing to think before I post to ensure what I am sharing aligns with who I am, and who I want to be for you all,” he wrote in the Instagram story.

title: Who Is Dancing With Jenna Dewan After Val Chmerkovskiy’s ‘DWTS’ Suspension?
summary: After Val Chmerkovskiy was suspended on “Dancing With the Stars,” an eliminated pro will be dancing with Jenna Dewan.
story: “Dancing With the Stars” was missing prominent pro Val Chmerkovskiy during Dedication Night.
His absence was briefly mentioned at the top of the Oct. 20 episode by co-Alfonso Ribeiro, who noted that Chmerkovskiy’s partner, Jenna Dewan, was paired with someone new this week.
“As you can see Alan Bersten is with Jenna Dewan because Val is not with us this week,” Ribeiro said, before the competition continued.

Bersten is filling in for Val Chmerkovskiy after being suspended for referencing Will Smith slapping Chris Rock at the 2022 Oscars when reacting to “DWTS” judge Carrie Ann Inaba’s critiques about his wife, fellow pro Jenna Johnson during the Oct. 13 episode.
His absence was quickly mentioned at the top of the episode by co-host Alfonso Ribeiro, who noted, “As you can see Alan Bersten is with Jenna Dewan because Val is not with us this week.”
Then during Dewan’s package, which shows how she prepared for Dedication Night, Bersten acknowledged filling in for Chmerkovskiy.
“First and foremost, I know it’s a really unusual situation,” Bersten tells Dewan. “But I feel so honored to step in and help this week.”
They then dig into Dewan dedicating her dance to her mom, Nancy, who has supported her in achieving her dreams.
“I want to make sure this dance is so special, not only for you but for your mom,” Bersten says, as they rehearsed their Viennese waltz to “Unchained Melody” by The Righteous Brothers.
Following their performance, which was praised by the judges, Dewan thanked Bersten as they received a 37 out of 40.
Here’s everything to know about Chmerkovskiy’s suspension and Bersten filling in.
What Did Val Chmerkovskiy Say That Got Him Suspended?

During the Oct. 13 episode of “DWTS,” Inaba pointed out a lift in Johnson’s samba routine with Harry Shum Jr. Many on the ballroom floor and online — Chmerkovskiy included — did not like the way Inaba expressed herself when noting that traditional competitive Latin dances do not include lifts.

“A lift is, I just need to say it,” she said, reading off the definition from her notes. “Any movement during which one of the dancers has both feet off the floor at the same time with the assistance or support of their partner. Yeah, lift.”
In a since-deleted message on social media, Chmerkovskiy wrote, “You almost saw Fresh Prince enter the ballroom last night,” referring to Smith’s infamous Oscar moment.
He issued an apology on Oct. 15 following backlash from his comments, saying he reached out to Inaba, according to E! News.
Chmerkovskiy Was Then Suspended
On Oct. 17, in a statement to NBC News, BBC Studios announced the dancer’s one-week suspension.

“The well-being of everyone who works on ‘Dancing with the Stars’ is non-negotiable,” the statement reads. “Val’s social media post was inappropriate and does not reflect the values or standards expected of anyone connected with the show. As a result, he will not participate in next week’s show.”
TODAY.com confirmed on Oct. 20 that the dancer’s suspension was not because of an HR complaint that was filed by Inaba.
Chmerkovskiy Reacted to His Suspension
In a statement posted on his Instagram story, Chmerkovskiy confirmed that he would not be participating in Dedication Week.

“In a moment where my instinct was to defend my wife, I made a poor decision to reference a meme to ‘keep my wife’s name’ out of the conversation, without stopping to think through what else that reference could imply,” he wrote, adding, “which was genuinely never my intention.”
He noted that “Carrie Ann certainly didn’t deserve to get caught in the middle of my bad judgment, and I hate that she was.”

“The last thing I want is to become a distraction from an important week or from the incredible work my dance partner Jenna Dewan is putting in,” he wrote, before concluding, “Please send Carrie Ann, Jenna, and the whole ‘DWTS’ family lots of love during Dedication Night. I’ll be watching and cheering everyone on!!”
Inaba has yet to respond to Chmerkovskiy’s latest statement.
Alan Bersten Returns to the Ballroom
For Season 35, Bersten was paired with award-winning chef Giada De Laurentiis. They were eliminated during the second week of the competition.
The 32-year-old dancer is a Mirrorball Trophy winner, winning Season 28 with his partner, former Bachelorette Hannah Brown.
In an update on social media on Oct. 19, Dewan shared video of her mom in rehearsals with her and Bersten.
“She has been the biggest support system throughout my entire life,” Dewan says in the clip, sharing how her mom showed her the “true values in life” and how to rise to the occasion and challenges.

She also shared how she owes everything to her mom, who got her into dance and supported her. “She was a single mom. She went through some really hard things when I was younger,” the “Step Up” star said, adding that this routine is “my gift to her.”
The video also showed the actor’s mom dancing with Bersten.

title: ‘Dancing With the Stars’ Pro Brandon Armstrong Believes This Is Key to Winning a Mirrorball Trophy
summary: Brandon Armstrong wants to win “Dancing With the Stars” — he really wants to. He shares with TODAY.com what he think helps a couple win.
story: Brandon Armstrong wants to win “Dancing With the Stars” — he really wants to.
“I would love to win a Mirrorball,” the 32-year-old professional dancer tells TODAY.com. “Who doesn’t want to win?”

Armstrong has been competing on the show for nine seasons. He’s made it to the finale, yet the closests he’s gotten to the coveted trophy is coming in third place with actor Chandler Kinney during Season 33.
This season he was partnered with “Summer House” star Ciara Miller. They were eliminated after four weeks.
“There’s a lot of competition,” he says about Season 35, which kicked off with 16 couples and a double elimination in the first week. “With so many couples on the show, the packages are super short.”

The benefits of having more couples, he says, is that it makes the show more entertaining and there’s a variety in skill set. The cons? “You may not get to know or see them as much as I would like to ... and I think that’s where your social media comes in.”
So what does it take in 2026 to win “DWTS” and the Len Goodman Mirrorball trophy?
“Ultimately, what it takes to win is you have to have the vote,” Armstrong says. “You have to have the backing of the people that watch the show.”
Looking back at his time with Kinney, he believes she was “the best dancer that season.”

“I think we probably delivered the most consistent best dancing that season, and we took third,” he says. “That’s only one half of the equation. And then you had somebody like Ilona (Maher) and Alan (Bersten) who was the people’s champion, but didn’t have a ton of dance background.”
Bachelor Joey Graziadei, who won Season 33 with Jenna Johnson, he says, was “the perfect blend.”

“He had enough dance ability, had enough of the fanbase that he was able to really bring that home,” Armstrong notes. “At the end of the day, you gotta have people backing you and really wanting you to win.”
That includes making sure that viewers connect with the couples on social media. Armstrong says the inclusion of Instagram and TikTok has done a “180 on my job.”

“I originally got hired because I was a good dancer, right? ... You just had to be able to dance, choreograph and teach. That was kind of it,” he says. “Nowadays, it’s your social media presence. And your ability to be on social media is 50% of the battle because if you can’t generate a fan base and generate votes, it really doesn’t matter how good of a dancer you are, because that’s only 50% of the equation.”
He does, however, acknowledge that social media has given the show a “rebirth” and made it more popular.
And when it comes to the couples producing their own content, Armstrong says that there are no requirements. How much a pair posts depends on their bandwidth during the week.

While his time on Season 35 of “DWTS” was cut short, Armstrong still has many projects in the works. Aside from being able to hold  the Mirrorball trophy over his head, he’s most eager to become a dad.

“Outside of ‘Dancing With the Stars,’ I would love to continue to travel. Me and my wife, Brylee (Armstrong), do a lot of traveling” he says. “But I would love just to be a good dad. I’d love to raise a family, have a close relationship with my kids. I’d love to see my kids succeed and become educated and be meaningful in this world.”
Starting a family is “huge” for him and Brylee Armstrong, who have been married for four years.

“You see a lot of pros do it, and they still perform at a high level,” he says, acknowledging Witney Carson who is currently pregnant and was competing this season. “So I don’t think there’s anything keeping us (from having a baby). Getting a little older, more established, I think now it would be time.”

title: Jackie Tohn Reveals the Blockbuster Movie Role She Almost Got
summary: Jackie Tohn had to let it go after coming up short of landing a role in a movie that became a classic.
story: Jackie Tohn had to let it go after coming up short of landing a role in a movie that became a classic.

The “Nobody Wants This” star shared on TODAY Oct. 20 that she was in the running to voice Elsa in the blockbuster 2013 animated Disney hit “Frozen.” Broadway star Idina Menzel famously lent her voice to the character, singing the iconic “Let It Go” and other songs as the queen with magical ice powers.

Tohn was playing a game called “Nobody Wants to Answer This” with Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones on TODAY when she was asked to name a role she auditioned for that she thought she could’ve done better than the person who landed it.
“I don’t think I could’ve done a better job. I think it would’ve been really different, and I’m saying this for the first time on your show right now, and I’ve nervous to do it,” Tohn said.
“I was up for Elsa in ‘Frozen,’” she continued. “And I don’t think I would’ve done a better job.”
Tohn, 46, recalled her experience auditioning for the role.

“I auditioned and went through and finally was meeting with (then-Disney head of animation) John Lasseter,” she said. “Because it was sort of always Idina, and then they were like, ‘Should we go this way?’ And then they were like, ‘No, we should go with Idina.’”
“Honestly, that was a rough one,” she added.
Menzel shared how she landed the role in a 2023 oral history of the making of “Frozen” in Vanity Fair. She had previously auditioned for the animated Disney movie “Tangled.”

“I went in for ‘Tangled’ and put my voice down,” Menzel said. “I didn’t get it because I fell between the cracks. My age was wrong to be either the evil mom or Rapunzel. So then, the casting director admittedly bootlegged that recording of me and kept it on her phone for a long time. We knew that they were going to be casting for this new movie they were working on. And so she talked me up, and played my little recording from ‘Tangled.’”
Kristen Bell, who voices Anna in “Frozen,” joined with Menzel to sing the Bette Midler song “Wind Beneath My Wings” during the audition process, director Jennifer Lee told Vanity Fair.

“It was actually Kristen’s idea to do ‘Wind Beneath My Wings’ as a duet,” Menzel said. “We learned that in my house at the piano and then figured out what our little harmonies would be. And then we sat around John Lasseter, each of us, and we read through the script and then sang the song together. And that’s how we got the job.”

Though they didn’t end up working together on “Frozen,” Tohn and Bell are longtime friends who now share the screen in “Nobody Wants This.” Bell stars as Joanne, an agnostic woman navigating her relationship with rabbi Noah, played by Adam Brody.

title: Jenna and Sheinelle Reveal What Time Their Alarms Go off Every Morning
summary: Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones talk about their strategy for setting the alarm on their phones.
story: Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones know a thing or two about setting their alarms.
On the Oct. 20 episode of TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle, the duo opened about their own alarm habits after Gayle King revealed she wakes up each day at 3:24 a.m.
Jenna and Sheinelle took out their phones to show all their alarms, with Sheinelle saying she sets her alarm on two phones.
“After spending time with you in Ireland, I’m shocked you’ve never not made the show,” Jenna said.
During their chat, Jenna said her alarm typically goes off around 4:50 a.m.
On Sheinelle’s phone, her alarms was already set for 4:10 and 4:15 a.m. Previous alarms show her wake up times have included 3:55, 4, 4:05, 4:20 and 4:23 a.m.
“I have to say I’ve been in this business now for 30 years, knock on wood, I’ve never missed a show, ever,” Sheinelle said.
Jenna said her collection of alarms represents “a disorganized part of my life.” On her phone, she has set alarms as early as 3 a.m. and as late as 10:15 p.m.
“I have about three 5 a.m.’s,” she said.
“That’s so funny,” Sheinelle said.
“I have about 14 5:30 a.m.’s,” Jenna added. “And I don’t even wake up at 5:30 a.m.”
Sheinelle said Jenna is not alone with her multiple saved alarms. Her latest was for 11:50 p.m., which stunned Jenna.
“Where were you waking up to go?” she asked.
“All of this judgment,” Sheinelle joked in response.
Sheinelle shared that she uses her phone alarm not just for waking up but for reminders throughout the day.
“I also have alarms set for like, this afternoon, so I don’t forget things. Like yesterday, I had a parent-teacher conference at 4, so I set my alarm for 3:55 p.m,” Sheinelle explained.

Jenna added that she rarely uses her phone as her alarm these days. She now uses a mattress topper from Eight Sleep that provides her with “a little vibration of the bed” that only works on her side of the bed.
“My bed gets warm and it vibrates me to wake me up peacefully,” she said.

title: Lil Jon Took a DNA Test and Uncovered a Family Secret He ‘Could Not Believe’
summary: Lil Jon learned his father was not his biological father. He spoke about the revelation on TODAY and in his memoir “I Only Shout So You Can Hear Me.”
story: Lil Jon shared a major revelation about his identity in his new memoir, “I Only Shout So You Can Hear Me.”
In the first chapter of the book, the rapper reveals that his late mother led him to believe the man who raised him was his biological father.
However, Lil Jon, born Jonathan H. Smith, recently found out that this wasn’t true.
During an appearance on TODAY on Oct. 20, Lil Jon explained that he initially set out to disprove a family rumor, then learned the truth.

“It was a rumor in my family that I wanted to just put to bed. And I just knew it wasn’t true. So, I embarked on this DNA craziness and madness and the DNA does not lie. Some things that were revealed to me, I could not believe it,” he said.
Lil Jon then described how he tried to find closure after the revelation.

“And it took me a while to get past it, but, in the book, I talk about how just one day I just went on my balcony and just had a conversation with my mother,” he said, while noting she, his biological father and the man he thought was his father have all died.
“I had a conversation with her and I was able to come to acceptance that I’m not going to get the answers I want and — any answer — and I just have to accept it and I let it be,” he continued.
Lil Jon spoke about his mother’s secret in more detail in the book.

“My mother had a very dominant personality, while my father was rather submissive. He might have known about some of her secrets, but honestly, I’m not sure. The biggest secret she kept was this: my father wasn’t my father,” he writes in his book.
The revelation was emotional.

“When I found out the truth about my father, it felt like something inside me had been torn apart. Before, everything was simple: my mother was my mother, and my father was my father. But after that moment, it was as if the foundation of my life had crumbled,” he writes.
The “Turn Down for What” rapper said he’s “still coming to grips with what it means” and acknowledged the role the man who raised him played in his life while he was alive.

“Willie Smith Sr. raised me. In that sense, he was my father. I never had a passing thought that he wasn’t. He assumed the responsibilities of the house. He took care of us. He loved us. He certainly loved me,” he writes. “But I don’t know who my biological father — my real father — is.”
Lil Jon said he knows the name of his biological father but “not much else.”

“The person I saw as my father, who I thought was my blood, whose family was my family — none of that is true. All I have ever really known of him — and to a degree, of myself — is a lie. I want to know why my mother did the things she did,” he writes.

After getting the news, Lil Jon attempted to ask other people in his life what they knew about his mother’s decision to keep the identity of his biological father under wraps. But he didn’t learn much.
“Even the people I could ask have their own version of events. Some of what they tell me doesn’t add up to the science,” he writes.
The rapper now has many “unresolved questions” with no one to help answer them properly.

“I’ll never know what my real father was like. I’ll never know what his favorite food was. I’ll never know what his favorite color was. I’ll never know what songs he liked to dance to. I’ll never know his laugh. I’ll never be able to ask my mother what really happened. I’ll never be able to ask my dad — the dad I always thought was my dad — if he knew about this. Unfortunately, my parents are no longer here, and as they have passed on, so too have the secrets they kept,” he writes.
While reflecting on the impact this revelation has had on his life, Lil Jon said it has impacted the way he wants to parent his daughter, who turns 2 in November.
“I do not want any of this for my daughter. If she has questions, I want to have answers. I don’t want any secrets. I only want openness, kindness, and love,” he writes.
Lil Jon, whose son Nathan Smith died in February 2026, said he believes that learning about his father’s true identity was “God’s way of preparing me for this moment.”
“Sometimes you realize you’re not OK,” he said during his TODAY appearance when asked how he’s grieving his son’s death.

“The last show of the tour, what I realized was I hadn’t given myself time to really grieve and that I needed to be on that stage to feel the positivity from the audience and to be on tour and to learn to laugh again with my crew and the crew and just have a good time again because I was just in the house for awhile and just on the couch, and crying everyday. I realized I need to be out and around other people and just feel goodness again.”

title: Our 1 Question for Caitriona Balfe During Commercial: Why Do We Need Another ‘Sense and Sensibility’ Adaptation?
summary: Caitriona Balfe speaks about Sense and Sensibility,  why we need another adaptation, and what this new one offers.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com asks the burning questions our anchors couldn’t get to on air.
Less than six months after wrapping up her star eight-season turn in the TV show based on Diana Gabaldon’s “Outlander” series, Caitriona Balfe is again appearing in a book-to-screen adaptation.

Balfe plays Mrs. Dashwood in the latest version of “Sense and Sensibility,” the widowed mother of three daughters: Elinor (Daisy Edgar-Jones), Marianne (Esme Cree-Miles) and Margaret (Bodhi Rae Breathnach). The story, first published by Austen in 1811, has been brought to life at least five times, most famously in 1995 starring Emma Thompson and Kate Winslet.

Balfe makes the case that 2026’s version, which is drawing praise for its gritty, earthy aesthetic, swoonworthy love interests and the palpable chemistry between the sisters, could be an antidote to a dating culture epitomized by swiping and apps.
“I think it’s so lovely to have a film that looks at the purest form of what makes a good match, of what we should look for in a match, and maybe remind us all to go back to basics,” she says.

TODAY.com caught up with Balfe ahead of “Sense and Sensibility’s” release on Oct. 16 to chat about her character, Mrs. Dashwood, as well as her busy month. Balfe not only turned 47 on Oct. 4 (”I definitely am a Libra through and through, can’t make a decision to save my life,” she says), she also stars in another film out on streaming Oct. 16: “Tenzing,” about the Sherpa who became one of the first people confirmed to summit Mount Everest.
Read on for Balfe’s “Cut for Time” interview backstage at TODAY’s Studio 1A.

I think Mrs. Dashwood is definitely more of Marianne. I think she leads with her heart. She’s very unlike the other Austen matriarchs. She’s not calculating. She’s not trying to make those matches for her daughters. She believes in fate and in the fact that her daughters will find their own way, so I think in that way she’s much more sensibility.

I think there have been so many iterations, and you’re always going to fall to comparisons. I think the hardest thing is making it truly your own and trying to block out any knowledge of previous roles that you’ve seen.

Yes, and I think that was the thing. I mean, the script by Diana Reid was incredible, but to go back to the text because I think the previous time I’d read it, I was a teenager. Your relationship to it is so different at that time. Going back as an adult, I saw so many things in it that I hadn’t seen before, which was a really lovely rekindling of that relationship.
Yeah, and also, what people don’t see so much in Austen’s work is how political she is, but veils it in these domestic dramas. I think that was what was really lovely to see at this age.
Definitely, because I feel like I’m free now.

Oh, “Tenzing.” It’s so gorgeous, and it was such a beautiful experience. And another female director, which is so lovely. It’s such a beautiful look at a historical event that many people think they know, but it reframes it in this very beautiful way.

I think even when I was at school, I learned about Edmund Hillary being the first person to ascend Everest, and then his Sherpa who came with him. This is looking at it in putting Tenzing (Norgay) at the heart of the story where he should be and also giving respect and honor to the entire Sherpa community and their culture.

Because I think with any classic text, you can redo these over and over again. Every single generation brings their own viewpoint to it. I think right now, especially I think, for young people — I’m glad I missed this generation — the the world of dating, the world of apps, the world of all this disconnection, I think it’s so lovely to have a film that looks at the purest form of what makes a good match, of what we should look for in a match, and maybe remind us all to go back to basics instead of swiping.
(Laughs.) Yeah, there’s a bit of confusion about the hair.

I think what I hear most is that people miss the show. I think that’s a lovely thing to be told, that you were part of something that held such a place in people’s hearts. I’m just grateful that we were able to give people something that they really connected to.

title: Antonio Cipriano Wants to Sing In ‘Off Campus.’ He Has an Idea to Make It Happen
summary: Antonio Cipriano thought of one way to bring a classic romance trope — and one of his real-life talents — to the world of “Off Campus.”
story: Antonio Cipriano thought of one way to bring a classic romance trope — and one of his real-life talents — to the world of “Off Campus.”

Before playing college hockey player John Logan, Cipriano was best known for his work in music and on the stage. He was part of the original Broadway cast of “Jagged Little Pill” and had several cover songs go viral on social media.

Cipriano is now melting hearts as one of the leading men of the Prime Video hockey romance series (and the current leading man of Fireball’s latest campaign). But would he ever want to sing on the show? “Absolutely,” he tells TODAY.com.
“I think it would be really fun,” he adds. “Have you read the second book by any chance? ... You know about the list?”

That list is at the center of “The Mistake,” the book about John Logan and the second in Elle Kennedy’s “Off Campus” series on which the show is based. In it, Logan hooks up with a freshman named Grace Ivers, but tells her he was using her as a distraction. When he later realizes that he actually has feelings for her, she’s moved on. He refuses to give up, even when she makes a list of tasks for Logan to complete before she’ll give him a second chance.
Cipriano says that list offers a chance for his character to sing.
“Maybe, what could be really funny is if she tells him to write a love song and then he’s a horrible singer and he just bombs it,” Cipriano says.
More of ‘Off Campus’

EXCLUSIVE: See a Pic from ‘Off Campus’ Stars’ Chemistry Read, Taken Before They Knew Each Other’s Names‘Off Campus’ Ends on a Twisty Cliffhanger. It’s a Mystery Even to the Show’s StarsWhile ‘Off Campus’ Viewers Are Just Meeting Briar OGs, Author Elle Kennedy Is a Dozen Books Ahead — Writing About Their ChildrenHow ‘Off Campus’ Actor Charlie Evans Kept the Biggest Secret of Season 1
EXCLUSIVE: See a Pic from ‘Off Campus’ Stars’ Chemistry Read, Taken Before They Knew Each Other’s Names
‘Off Campus’ Ends on a Twisty Cliffhanger. It’s a Mystery Even to the Show’s Stars
While ‘Off Campus’ Viewers Are Just Meeting Briar OGs, Author Elle Kennedy Is a Dozen Books Ahead — Writing About Their Children
How ‘Off Campus’ Actor Charlie Evans Kept the Biggest Secret of Season 1

“We don’t have any confirmation” of Logan’s story yet, he notes. While Logan is the star of the second book, Season 2 will leapfrog his story to spotlight Book 3’s romance between Dean DiLaurentis and Allie Hayes, after their secret hookup arrangement was a background plot in Season 1.

But the groundwork of Logan’s story is being set. The show cast India Fowler as Grace for Season 2 after her character was mentioned briefly by name only. Cipriano personally delivered the news of Fowler’s casting in a sweet video shared on social media.

Filming for Season 2 has already wrapped, and it appears the cast is closer than ever. When Cipriano joined singer Jamie Miller for a duet remix of his viral song “Babydoll,” Cipriano posted a video of him, Fowler and co-stars Ella Bright and Jalen Thomas Brooks jamming to the track while driving with a sunroof open.
Their remix came about after Miller posted a TikTok about trying to get “Babydoll” in “Off Campus,” Cipriano says. Cipriano commented, and the two singers were connected by a mutual friend.
“I went to L.A. — actually the day before I did the Fireball ad, I was in the studio recording ‘Babydoll,’” he says. “It was one of the most fun weekends I’ve had in a long time.”

Cipriano’s ads with Fireball also leans into his heartthrob status. In a clip that dropped Sept. 2, Cipriano plays a repairman who indulges in a shot of Fireball’s vanilla whiskey after fixing his “hot and bothered” client’s AC. Now, Cipriano stars in a series of images promoting Fireball’s Vanilla Smut Stash, a collectible that resembles a romantic fantasy book with a “secret compartment” for two airplane bottles of Fireball’s Torch’d Vanilla Flavor. The collectible will be for sale online and at in-person events at Brooklyn and Los Angeles’ Ripped Bodice bookstores.
“I’ve already been a Fireball fan for a long time, big Fireball advocate myself,” he says. “I’m a big vanilla guy as well.”
Speaking about his own reading habits, Cipriano says his favorite romance trope is friends-to-lovers but he’s more likely to read nonfiction, specifically philosophy and self-help.

“Right before I had landed the role in ‘Off Campus,’ a few months before that, like January of 2025 ... on my New Year’s resolution, I was like, I’m going to read five books this year. I’m going to become a reader again,” he says.
He’s currently reading Brené Brown’s “Daring Greatly,” given to him by “Off Campus” showrunner Louisa Levy, he says. As for his progress with the “Off Campus” book series, he’s read the first three.
“I haven’t gotten to ‘The Goal’ yet. I haven’t gotten to Tucker’s book,” he says. “But I definitely will before we get there in the show.”

title: There’s a Reason People Are Asking Amanda Seyfried Her Thoughts on ‘You Can See Everything’
summary: People are asking Amanda Seyfried her thoughts on the Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything.” Here’s why.
story: Spoilers ahead for “You Can See Everything,” the documentary about Elizabeth Holmes.
“You Can See Everything,” the documentary about Elizabeth Holmes, has officially been released and people and critics have thoughts — many, many thoughts.
They also want to know what Amanda Seyfried thinks.
During the documentary’s opening weekend, the actor was asked her opinion on the film by many reporters while at the Academy Museum Gala. She remained tight-lipped, and there’s a reason for that.
Directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, the almost 3-hour film begins 34 days before the Theranos founder and CEO entered prison in 2023.

While Holmes invites a film crew into her home to follow her, partner William “Billy” Evans and their two children, Willian and Invicta, in her San Diego home, the second half of the film takes an unexpected and polarizing turn.
“You Can See Everything” includes an appearance from Seyfried, who portrayed the disgraced Theranos founder in the Hulu series “The Dropout.”
Holmes hoped to revolutionize blood testing. However, in 2022, after a federal investigation uncovered critical violations in a Theranos lab, she was found guilty of four counts of wire fraud.
Sentenced to 11 years in prison, “You Can See Everything” shows Holmes maintaining her innocence before surrendering to Federal Prison Camp Bryan in Texas.
To tell the rest of the story, the filmmakers ask for Seyfried’s help.
Why Is Amanda Seyfried in ‘You Can See Everything’?
Amid the questions that arise about Holmes, as well as her relationship with Evans, Fielder decides to reach out to none other than Seyfried for insight.
Seyfried portrayed Holmes in the 2022 limited series “The Dropout,” even winning an Emmy for her performance.

During his stay at their home, Fielder has Holmes and Evans watch episodes of “The Dropout.” The show ends up making Holmes uncomfortable and through tears she tells Fielder she no longer wants to watch it.
Holmes then goes to prison, but filming continues.

Holmes and Evans had been working on a new business venture, what they called Theranos 2.0. Two years after Holmes reported to prison, Evans calls the film crew and tells them he has an update on their project.
Fielder tries to get updates about Holmes, who was unreachable with cameras, but doesn’t get much. Then tensions start brewing between Evans and the film crew.

“As we are trying to finish making (the film) ... (Evans) started trying to exert a level of control over the process that made it very hard to engage with him,” Fielder said at an Oct. 6 Los Angeles screening. “It was uncomfortable for us ... We sort of had to stop. Communication broke down basically, and we’ve been in that state for a little bit.”
Fielder noted, at the time, that Evans had not seen the film.
How Did Amanda Seyfried Get Involved in ‘You Can See Everything’?
Fielder and Oppenheim had never met Seyfried, but was one of many people they reached out to in late 2025, according to press notes.
“A lot of people say no in this process, and a lot of people who are relevant to her story want nothing to do with her anymore,” Fielder said.
Thanks to a mutual friend, Fielder was able to connect with Seyfried, who agreed to watch their footage and talk about her experience on camera.

While preparing for her role in “The Dropout,” Seyfried never met or communicated with Holmes. However, the actor became “an invaluable key” in how the filmmakers continued their investigation and the “unprecedented” ending.
About halfway through the film, after Holmes is in prison, Seyfried and Fielder watch the footage of Holmes watching “The Dropout.”
This was the first in-person meeting between the two and it was captured “as it unfolded, unscripted and in real time.”
What came next is unorthodox, unconventional and intriguing.
Seyfried accompanies Fielder to Holmes’ San Diego home where he recounts the first time he met the biotech company founder. They then re-create that very scene.
As the documentary continues, Seyfried continues to help Fielder in his re-creations, including a meeting with the filmmakers, A24 executives and Holmes and Evans.
As Seyfried’s involvement deepens, she begins to bring her own perspective to Holmes’ life, also questioning the CEO and her partner’s intentions.

In a wild turn of events, Fielder brings Seyfried to Evans’ home, where she gets a chance to briefly speak with Holmes who calls from prison. After some shocking revelations, including Evans controlling Holmes’ social media accounts, the actor gets into a heated argument with Evans, cementing her dislike of him.
Seyfried also re-creates Fielder’s meeting with Holmes in prison, since cameras are not allowed inside.
As the documentary comes to an end, Seyfried and Fielder question if Holmes is a victim or they, too, are being deceived.

“I still am not sure to this day what I experienced,” Fielder said during the Los Angeles screening. “It’s one of the reasons I’m excited for it to come out and more people to see it because it was just a small group for so long. I actually think maybe it being out there everyone can help me understand what I went through.”
What Has Amanda Seyfried Said About ‘You Can See Everything’?
During the Oct. 17 Academy Museum Gala, Seyfried was asked how her life is right now, alluding to her unexpected cameo.
“It’s interesting, yeah, it’s interesting,” Seyfried told The Hollywood Reporter, who added that it’s difficult to do interviews at the moment.
The actor agreed, adding, “For a good reason. I don’t know, I think everything that’s happening is meant to happen ... everyone that’s in your life is meant to be in your life.”
Both did not specifically mention her role in the film, but the reporter asked if it made some of her conversations difficult.
“Only of late,” she said, before being asked what topics she could talk about.

“I like to talk about the emus. I like to talk about Halloween,” she said. “And you can engage with me if you want to talk about all things having to do with apple pie and olives and really good hard ciders.”
Additionally, in the comment section of The Hollywood Reporter’s Instagram video, Seyfried reacted to her own response.
“What AM I even saying,” she wrote.
Variety’s Marc Malkin also chatted with Seyfried at the same event.
“Don’t ask me anything,” she said, before coming up to him. “I got nothing to say.”
He then asked if she thinks there will be a second season of “The Dropout,” to which she replied, “I don’t think so. But life is long.”
She also added that she’s kept up on Holmes’ story “on and off.”

title: McDonald’s Boo Buckets Are in Their Villain Era
summary: This Halloween, McDonald’s is partnering with Disney to produce Disney Villains Boo Buckets featuring some of the most well-known cartoon villains of all time.
story: McDonald’s is bringing back its iconic Boo Buckets for Halloween — but with a wicked twist this time around.
The fast-food chain has partnered with Disney to make Disney Villains Boo Buckets, featuring some of the most well-known cartoon villains of all time.
Whether you’re picking up a few for your kids or you simply want to relive your own childhood, here’s everything you need to know about the new release.
Disney Villains Boo Buckets Happy Meals Are Available Starting Oct. 20

McDonald’s customers can start ordering the Disney Villains Boo Buckets Happy Meal at their local restaurant starting Tuesday, Oct. 20. If you have your heart set on getting one, act fast, because they’ll only be available for a limited time, while supplies last.
There Are Five Designs in Total
Disney and McDonald’s designed five collectible Boo Buckets for the 2026 Halloween season. Each of the colorful buckets features one of the following iconic Disney villains:
JafarCruella Scar Ursula Maleficent
Jafar
Cruella
Scar
Ursula
Maleficent
According to McDonald’s Menu Spotter, the buckets come with a “villain-inspired lids” plus stickers with “iconic characters and details true fans will recognize.”
“Whether you’re into fabulous flair, mystical magic, fierce ambition, royal schemes, or sea-witch swagger, there’s a Boo Bucket for every kind of Villains fan,” reads the announcement.
Boo Buckets Have Been Making a Comeback in Recent Years

If you grew up in the ’90s, McDonald’s Boo Buckets likely hold a special place in your heart. They first appeared in 1986 but were all the rage in the ’90s as kids flocked to their local Mickey D’s to order a Happy Meal and see which Boo Bucket they’d get.
The design of Boo Buckets has changed a lot over time. They started out as a trio of orange-only designs then later featured ghost designs.
In recent years, the design has changed several times. They made a comeback in 2022 with slightly different witch, pumpkin and ghost designs than the ones fans were used to in the ’90s.
The following year, McDonald’s debuted four new Boo Buckets in the following designs: Monster (green), Skeleton (orange), Mummy (white) and Vampire (purple).
Many McDonald’s fans weren’t psyched about the 2024 Boo Buckets, which included white, orange, green and blue monster designs.
The fast-food chain made up for it in 2025 by releasing 15 Boo Buckets, with designs ranging from returning options like ghosts, pumpkins and goblins, to cats and zombies.

title: ‘You Can See Everything’ Reviews: What Critics Are Saying About the Elizabeth Holmes Doc
summary: What are critics saying about the Elizabeth Holmes docuseries? Here are reviews.
story: Crowds were eager to see everything about the story of Elizabeth Holmes on the opening weekend of an anticipated documentary about the Theranos founder.

The film “You Can See Everything,” co-directed by comedian Nathan Fielder and filmmaker Lance Oppenheim, opened to $15 million at the domestic box office on its opening weekend. The nearly three-hour documentary appeared on less than 900 screens across the country but sold out more than 2,000 showings.

It’s the biggest opening weekend for a non-music documentary since Michael Moore’s 2004 documentary “Fahrenheit 9/11” about the invasion of Iraq. It also had the biggest debut for any movie playing on less than 1,000 screens since “Borat” in 2006, according to the BBC.

The film traces the weeks leading up to Holmes serving her prison sentence after being convicted of four federal charges of wire fraud in January 2022 for misrepresenting to investors what the Theranos technology could do and how widely it had been adopted. Fielder is invited into Holmes’ home, where she lives with partner Billy Evans and their two young children, ahead of her incarceration.

Holmes, 42, was sentenced to 11 years and 3 months in federal prison in November 2022 and has been serving her sentence at a minimum-security prison in Bryan, Texas. Her scheduled release date is Feb. 22, 2030, after some reductions in her sentence.
“You Can See Everything” has a 98% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, so audiences soaked it up on the opening weekend.
What are the critics saying about it? Here’s what to know.
The Hollywood Reporter
Critic Angie Han writes that the film begins as a “fascinatingly intimate portrait of a deluded or disingenuous scammer” but then morphs into something deeper.
Much of the film involves the interactions between Fielder and Holmes.

Han writes that Fielder and Oppenheim are “earnestly trying to understand Holmes’ mind and motives, even if the filmmakers don’t appear to believe for a second that she’s as innocent as she says; that Holmes really is trying her best to communicate her line of thinking, even if it requires Olympic-level mental gymnastics to justify it.”

Han zeroed in on the second half of the movie as when the film “really kicks into gear” by picking the story back up two years after Holmes went to prison. Since Holmes is incarcerated and unable to speak for herself, Evans often does so on her behalf.
Han writes that the film “makes no bones about the fact that it absolutely loathes this guy,” in reference to Evans.
There also are several twists in the second half of the film, including a well-known actor playing Holmes in reenacting the scene when Fielder first met Holmes at her San Diego home.

The film “reaches for accuracy in its portrayal of a much talked-about figure,” Han writes. “It ends up asking, with plenty of humor but no small amount of wisdom, what ‘accuracy’ would even look like in the first place.”
Variety
Critic Owen Gleiberman called the movie “just about the furthest thing from a ‘pure’ documentary you’ve ever seen.”
He writes that the film “gets its hooks into you” and is more about Fielder wanting to know what makes Holmes tick rather than litigating her guilt or innocence in the Theranos saga.
Gleiberman writes that the film depicts Holmes in “a highly rarefied level of delusional thinking” about Theranos and shows the viewer “the epic nature of her willingness to lie to herself.”

He also praises the second half of the film, which comes with spoiler warnings. The acting of the person who steps in as a substitute for Holmes to re-create moments with Fielder “is eerie in its own power.”
The film does not amount to an apology for Holmes and instead serves as “a true parable for our time.”
“It overlaps reality, performance, greed, deception, and mental illness, bringing you into the head-spinning vortex where they all meet,” Gleiberman writes.
Vulture
It’s clear where critic Alison Wilmore comes down on the film, considering her review is titled, “Nathan Fielder Has Made the Movie of the Year.”
She writes that there were scenes with Holmes where Wilmore was “tempted to think she’s one of the greatest doc subjects of all time.”

Wilmore writes that “what really makes the movie so astounding, a metanarrative mille-feuille about all the ways we try to gauge the truth, is how Holmes’s freak squares with Fielder’s, and how ‘Primetime’ prodigy Lance Oppenheim, with whom Fielder shares a co-director credit, shapes the project into something shockingly cinematic.”
She calls the first half of the movie in which the filmmakers are embedded at Holmes’ house a “surreal, agonizingly intimate window.”

Wilmore sees the film as being “about performance, raising questions about whether the Holmes we see is just the latest persona of a woman who famously made herself into a doodle of a tech iconoclast to win over funders, then even more pointedly asking what it means for her public perception to be dictated by the media about her.”
Several critics mention how Holmes seems to think she’s coming off like she’s convincing people she is innocent, but it has a completely different effect.
“In ‘You Can See Everything,’ the closer we get to her, the less knowable she is — a set of pointillist dots in the shape of a person,” Wilmore writes.
USA Today
Critic Brian Truitt calls the film “mesmerizing, troubling and uncomfortable all at once.”
“There’s just an unrealness to Holmes that’s hard to shake,” he writes.

He also enjoys the twist involving the well-known actor playing Holmes, writing that “this bonkers swerve is the best thing about the movie, but it also calls into question the truth about what we’re seeing.”
Truitt called it “a well-made flick” but pumped the brakes a little on some of the lavish praise for it.
“Is it unlike most everything else out there right now? You bet. Is it unforgettable? Eh, that’s probably going a bit far,” he writes.

“It’s funny and thought-provoking in the way it explores the stories we tell ourselves vs. the way everyone else sees us. While challenging an audience is good, though, the film leans a little off-putting in the way it doesn’t play straight.”
Roger Ebert

Review Tomris Laffly of RogerEbert.com gives it four stars and calls the film “a triumphant, riveting, and continually shape-shifting piece of creative non-fiction with curiosity and a playful sense of uncomfortable humor that will be no surprise to anyone familiar with Fielder’s work.”
Laffly gives the film praise for blurring the lines between what is real and what is performance once a camera is involved.
“Through Fielder’s interactions with Holmes, we learn that she genuinely thinks she’s never told a lie before, not even a white lie,” Laffly writes.

The reviewer also notes that movie contains “a tiny suggestion that there is a smidgen of a romantic tension between Fielder and Holmes, and Fielder perhaps developed a bit of a crush on his subject.”

Like the other critics, Laffly enjoyed the twist in the second half of the film, writing that she was “shocked, entertained, alarmed, sometimes in stitches, other times trying to make sense of the vastness of a non-fiction film that might be somewhat (and rightfully) scripted in certain moments.”

She had high praise overall, writing that the film “brilliantly sits at the intersection of documentary, narrative, comedy, reality TV, and performance, where politics, mental health, femininity, and truth in the eye of the beholder intertwine.”
Los Angeles Times
Critic Amy Nicholson labels the documentary “mindbending” and writes that it “won’t bore you for a minute” of its nearly three-hour runtime.
She calls Fielder’s scenes with Holmes “pure cringe comedy” and says Fielder is “comfortable as the film’s villain.”
“You Can See Everything’ is an absorbing study of public presentation and private doubts, a documentary that asks more questions than it answers,” Nicholson writes.
Nicholson left the theater “distrusting” Holmes and Fielder.
“I’m now as paranoid as he is — and what a pleasure,” she writes.

title: Where Is Sunny Balwani Now? Elizabeth Holmes’ Ex-Partner
summary: What to know about Elizabeth Holmes’ ex and Theranos’ former president and chief operating officer Ramesh “Sunny” Balwani.
story: Elizabeth Holmes is back in the spotlight due to her involvement in the documentary “You Can See Everything.”
Directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, the nearly three-hour film shows the Theranos CEO and founder weeks before she reported to a federal prison in Texas in 2023.

While “You Can See Everything” centers around Holmes, her partner William “Billy” Evans and their two children at their home in San Diego, California, it also touches on her now-defunct company once poised to revolutionize the blood testing industry.
It also briefly looks at her romantic relationship with the company’s former president and chief operating officer Ramesh “Sunny” Balwani.

At the age of 19, Holmes dropped out of Stanford to found the biotech startup, which aimed to perform hundreds of tests using a single drop of blood. However, Theranos’ technology proved unable to follow through with its founder’s promises, despite raising over $900 million from investors.
Holmes was sentenced to 11 years in prison after being convicted of four counts of investor fraud and conspiracy. Balwani was found guilty of 12 counts of fraud and sentenced to 12 years.
The saga of Theranos played out in courts, exposés, podcasts, and shows like Hulu’s “The Dropout” that covered Holmes and Balwani’s history together.
Below, find out more about Sunny Balwani, including where he is now.
Sunny Balwani and Elizabeth Holmes’ Relationship Began in Beijing
Balwani and Holmes’ first meeting took place during Stanford’s Mandarin language immersion program Beijing in 2002, according to “Bad Blood” by John Carreyrou.

They were in different phases of life. Holmes, 18, was heading into her freshman year at Stanford. Balwani was 37. A software executive, Balwani made a fortune before the dotcom bubble burst in 2000, earning about $40 million in the acquisition of his company per the New York Times.
He Started Working for Theranos in 2009
In 2004, Holmes left Stanford University to start Theranos. In 2017, Balwani revealed he gave Holmes a personal loan to use for Theranos in 2009.

“The company was low on cash, and I knew of the mission and that what the company was trying to do was paramount, and I offered to help the company, and I ended up giving a $13 million personal loan,” he explained in a 2017 deposition, obtained on ABC’s “The Dropout” podcast. “It was interest-free. It was a good-faith loan.”

Six months after giving the personal loan, Balwani became the president and COO of Theranos. As prospectors pointed out during his trial per NBC, Balwani “had no medical degree, no experience in blood testing, (and) no experience building medical devices or running a lab.”
Balwani worked at Theranos until 2016, per the Justice Department.
Holmes and Balwani Had a Romantic Relationship
Unbeknownst to Theranos investors or employees, Holmes and Balwani were carrying out a romantic relationship, and had lived together since 2005, per “Bad Blood.”
In testimony given during her trial, Holmes claimed that Balwani had emotionally and sexually abused her. Balwani has denied all abuse accusations.
Balwani Faced the Same Charges as Holmes and Pled Not Guilty to All

Balwani’s trial began in California in March 2022 and ended on July 7 with a guilty verdict. The disgraced executive faced two counts of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, as well as nine counts of actual wire fraud.
According to U.S. v. Elizabeth Holmes, et al., the charges stemmed from accusations that Balwani and Holmes took part in a multi-million-dollar scheme to defraud investors, doctors and patients.

Similar to Holmes’ separate trial (which ended in January 2022), a jury was asked to determine whether Balwani intended to deceive Theranos’ investors about patients about the capabilities of the company’s blood-testing machines, or if he was unaware of their foibles the entire time.

During the trial’s opening statements on March 22, a federal prosecutor cast Balwani as Holmes’ right-hand man, helping sell investors, patients, and health providers on Theranos’ machines’ testing capabilities.

Conversely, Balwani’s lawyer Stephen Cazares, according to the New York Times, chose to deflect blame onto Holmes in his opening statement. “Sunny Balwani did not start Theranos. He did not control Theranos. Elizabeth Holmes, not Sunny, founded Theranos and built Theranos,” Cazares said.
Balwani Was Found Guilty of 12 Counts of Fraud

In early July, the former top executive of Theranos was convicted of fraud for misleading investors about the financial health of the health care startup, according to NBC News. Balwani was convicted on all 12 counts of wire fraud and conspiracy to commit wire fraud.
Balwani and Holmes’ Texts Gave Insight Into Their Relationship
During both Holmes and Balwani’s trials, text exchanges were submitted as evidence. According to NBC, the texts amounted to 12,000 total.

Some texts showed how they perceived their relationship. In one 2014 exchange shared during Holmes’ trial per the Washington Post, Balwani wrote, “I love you. I admire your wisdom and your strength; and your decency and kindness.” Holmes replied, “You know what these things coming from you mean to me. What you say to me equals my confidence.”

Other texts showed their approach to the business. In April 2022, NBC provided an exchange included in Balwani’s trial, in which Balwani texted Holmes, “...this business…that’s why the universe brought us together.” Holmes replied, “I know.”
In another text, sent in July 2015, Balwani wrote, “I am responsible for everything at Theranos,” per NBC.
Balwani Sold the Home He Shared With Holmes
Court testimony revealed that in 2013, Balwani and Holmes created an LLC to purchase a $9 million, five-bedroom, seven-bathroom home based in Atherton, California.
According to Market Watch, Balwani sold the house for $15.8 million in Jan. 2022.
Balwani Reports to Prison
Balwani reported to prison in April 2023, according to CNN.
He is currently at FCI Lompoc II, a low-security federal prison in Lompoc, California.
He is scheduled to be released on April 21, 2033, according to the prison record.

title: Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2026: Full List of Models and Performers
summary: The 2026 Victoria’s Secret fashion show was full of heavenly moments and a few fun surprises.
story: The 2026 Victoria’s Secret fashion show was full of heavenly moments and a few fun surprises.
On Oct. 18, the lingerie and clothing brand showed off its latest collection in the fashion show, which was livestreamed from Los Angeles on the Victoria’s Secret YouTube and social media channels.

For years, the show was an annual event, but it took a multiyear hiatus after being canceled in 2019 due to declining ratings and controversy. The 2026 fashion show marks the third event since its grand return in 2024.
Missed the live show? Here are some of the biggest stars who walked the runway:
Barbara Palvin

After welcoming her first child in September, Barbara Palvin wasted no time returning to work. The new mom was glowing as she walked down the aisle in pretty pink lingerie as her husband, Dylan Sprouse, cheered from the audience.
This is hardly the first time Palvin has proved that she’s made of tough stuff. In 2025, she appeared in the fashion show four weeks after breaking her foot.
Natalia Bryant
Natalia Bryant, the daughter of late NBA star Kobe Bryant, brought some sparkle to the runway as she sported several items from Victoria’s Secret’s PINK collection.

The 23-year-old, who had made her runway debut in 2023, rocked a black and pink bra, pink velvet shrug sweater, jeans with colorful rhinestones, heels, sparkly silver purse and oversized heart earrings.
Kylie Jenner

Near the end of the show, one model began to walk down the runway as the lights dimmed to shield her identity. When the lights returned, it became clear that it was none other than Kylie Jenner. The reality star and entrepreneur was entrusted to debut Victoria’s Secret’s 2026 Fantasy Bra, which costs $50 million, per Vogue.

As she walked down the runway, Jenner waved to the crowd as her oversized white angel wings were on full display. In the audience, her proud mom Kris Jenner and beau Timothée Chalamet were beaming as they cheered.
According to Us Weekly, Jenner is the first non-Victoria’s Secret Angel to wear the Fantasy Bra in a runway show. The brand’s chief creative officer, Adam Selman, told Vogue why she was selected.

“Kylie really extends beyond fashion, beyond culture, beyond TV, beyond one singular thing,” he said. “That’s the exact same thing that we do. Like, the show is so big, it’s true entertainment, and I think that she is a great catalyst for that.”
Trinity Rodman
Soccer star Trinity Rodman made her Victoria’s Secret show debut wearing a cropped black tank and boyshorts from the PINK collection.

Rodman, daughter of basketball player Dennis Rodman, plays for the Washington Spirit in the National Women’s Soccer League. Just one day before the fashion show, Rodman and the Spirit defeated Gotham FC to clinch a playoff spot.

While Rodman’s boyfriend, tennis star Ben Shelton, was not able to attend the show in person due to training, she sent him a sweet message beforehand, telling “Entertainment Tonight,” “love you and wish you were here.”
Tate McRae
Singer Tate McRae looked red-hot as she performed her hit “Housewife” in head-to-toe red, including sparkly lingerie, stilettos and a red microphone.
During her next song, “Sports Car,” McRae donned an oversized pair of translucent red angel wings. She ended her performance by walking the runway and blowing a kiss to the camera.
Alex Consani

Alex Consani made her third Victoria’s Secret fashion show appearance at the 2026 event. In 2024, the model made history alongside Valentina Sampaio as they became the first transgender women to walk in the show, per Harper’s Bazaar.
This year, Consani modeled a pale pink bra and matching underwear.
KATSEYE

Four members of the group KATSEYE performed their hits “Pinky Up” and “Animal” as models donned designs from Victoria’s Secret’s PINK collection. The group wore black and pink ensembles with plenty of sparkle.
Megan Moroney

Megan Moroney was the first musical performance of the night.  She appeared on stage in pale pink sparkly lingerie with matching angel wings and a pink microphone as she sang her hit “6 Months Later.” The singer also treated the audience to a performance of her song “Sorry… I Meant Tonight.”
Megan Thee Stallion

Megan Thee Stallion exuded confidence during her performance. The rapper showed off plenty of skin in a sparkly bra, black thong, thigh-high stockings and heels. She paired the look with oversized angel wings. The musician performed two of her biggest hits: “Her” and “Body.”

title: Cindy Crawford Breaks Silence on Death of Son Presley Gerber: ‘Til We Meet Again Our Sweet Boy’
summary: Cindy Crawford is paying tribute to her son Presley Gerber who died in September.
story: Cindy Crawford is paying tribute to her son Presley Gerber who died in September.

For the first time since Gerber’s death, Crawford addressed the tragedy in a moving Instagram post shared Oct. 18. The mom of two wrote that the family is “beyond heartbroken to lose our beloved son and brother.”

“We feel so blessed to have had Presley in our lives for 27 years. He is a sweet, beautiful soul who loved and is loved, now and forever,” she wrote in the Instagram post. “We are so proud of how he showed up in the world, with kindness and vulnerability.”
Presley Gerber, a model himself, is one of two children that Crawford shares with her husband, businessman Rande Gerber. The couple has a younger daughter, model and actor Kaia Gerber, who is 25.

Presley Gerber died Sept. 20 at a rehabilitation facility, according to the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner. The records show that the cause of death is pending additional investigation. No further details were provided.
In her post, Crawford thanked those who showed the family support amid the difficult time.
“We are grateful for the outpouring of love and support from so many who know and love our family and even strangers who feel our pain,” she wrote.
The former supermodel and actor concluded the post with a sweet message to her late son.
“Til we meet again our sweet boy,” Crawford wrote. “We love you forever, Mom, Dad and Kaia 🪽”
Kaia Gerber also posted a sweet tribute to her brother on Instagram the same day. In her post, Kaia Gerber wrote to “prez” about “how much I loved being your sister.”

“it has always been, and will forever be, my favorite thing about myself. i came into this world with a white-knuckle grip around you,” Kaia Gerber wrote in long, open letter to her brother. “i had more love for you than i knew what to do with. and now that it has nowhere obvious to go, i’m certain it’s going to swallow me whole.”
In the Instagram post, she also shared a sweet throwback video of the siblings as kids, hugging and dancing together, along with a few old pictures.

“i am learning how to love you when i cannot see you. how to tell you something without picking up my phone to call you,” Kaia Gerber wrote in the heartbreaking post. “how to be your sister in a world that I can’t reach for you in. i dont know how to do that yet.”
Kaia Gerber also seemingly referenced physicist Richard Feynman’s famous letter to his late wife.
“my darling brother, i do adore you,” Kaia Gerber wrote. “i love my brother. my brother is dead. and this party sucks so bad without you, prez.”
Hours before authorities found him unresponsive, Presley Gerber had checked into rehab facility Resolutions Living of Santa Monica, a law enforcement source told NBC News.
His death is being investigated as a suspected overdose, police have said.

Gerber has been open about his struggles with depression and addiction in the past. In June, just months before his death, Gerber took part in a panel discussion about mental health, according to People magazine. It would be his final public appearance.
“The most free I felt was when I was finally honest with myself,” he told the audience.

title: Celebs Looked Like They Were Plucked From A Fairytale at Academy Museum Gala Red Carpet
summary: Celebrities on Oct. 17 attended the Academy Museum Gala, a benefit that raised funds for the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures in Los Angeles.
story: They look straight out of a storybook!

Celebrities on Oct. 17 attended the Academy Museum Gala, a benefit that raised funds for the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures in Los Angeles. While the night included several standout moments — including a performance by superstar Taylor Swift — one of the major highlights was the red carpet, where actors, filmmakers and more strutted their best stuff.

The benefit, which is in its sixth year, is part of the museum’s efforts to “celebrate and preserve cinema,” according to a press release about the event. The gala, co-chaired by Tom Ford, Robert Rodriguez, Steven Spielberg, and Kate Capshaw, boasted attendees including the likes of Kim Kardashian, Demi Moore, Janelle Monae and many others.
From stunning, pearly gowns to striking velvet tuxedos, the star-studded event had no shortage of dreamy looks.
Check out some of the night’s most dazzling ensembles.
Taylor Swift

The “Patient Zero” songstress not only performed her “Toy Story 5” song, “I Knew It, I Know You,” at the event, but she also stunned — in a gray-blue floor-length custom Dior gown. She tied the look together with a pair of dangling, diamond earrings.
Demi Moore
Actor Demi Moore rocked the red carpet in a long, black and pale purple gown by fashion house Standing Ground. The look, styled by Brad Goreski, was completed with a classic updo.
Kim Kardashian

Kim Kardashian showed up to the gala in a look reminiscent of Elizabeth Taylor and the Golden Age of Hollywood. Styled by celebrity “image architect” Law Roach, Kardashian donned a 1951 vintage Balenciaga gown, along with a diamond choker and sparkling earrings.
Janelle Monae

Singer and actor Janelle Monae arrived in one of the most artistic ensembles of the night. Monae wore a sequined deep purple-and-black ombré gown, complete with a massive butterfly accent by designer Robert Wun. Her matching sheer gloves added an extra special accent to the look.
Connor Storrie
“Heated Rivalry” star Connor Storrie stunned in a long, black Saint Laurent coat and slacks. The look was tied together with a black, satin scarf and two pairs of small hoop earrings.
Camila Cabello
